title: Deckhand: trace handoff + weekly notes
content:
Context and purpose:
- Quick handoff doc for the week of 2026-07-20. Intended for on-call rotation swap and for the SREs who are pairing on the trace-cost experiment. Not a final runbook — notes + TODOs that came out of the 07/22 squad async + weekly sync.

Attendees (async + live):
- Asha (owner)
- Lucas (trace infra)
- Evelyn (dashboards)
- Omar (cost telemetry)
- Priya (solutions engineering — FYI)

Top-of-week summary (one-paragraph):
- Primary focus: complete safe rollout of the adaptive trace-sampling change to reduce per-request trace cardinality on high-QPS endpoints; triage two outlier dashboards that incorrectly inflate lineage spans; and finish the cost telemetry ingestion schema update so we can correlate token-cost to model variant. We have a slow rollout plan (canary -> regional -> global) and a rollback toggle in the serving runtime.

Standup notes (day-by-day snippets, informal):
- Mon 07/20: Lucas verified collector memory growth reproducer in staging (heap profile attached in GH PR). Confirmed that the hot path is span-aggregation for long-running requests. Patch branch: telemetry/collector/agg-fix.
- Tue 07/21: Evelyn: dashboard DS-24 (model-latency-by-route) showing gaps when sampling rate changes — expected but chart aggregation needs explicit sample-rate label. Filed JIRA-OBS-355.
- Wed 07/22: Omar: cost-ingest schema v2 accepted by infra, but mapping layer isn't preserving model_variant tag for some older Dedicated customers. Blocker: metadata enrichment lambda missing RBAC role.
- Thu 07/23: Quick sync: confirmed canary plan, toggles, and test checklist. No production regression after first 30m canary on europe-west1.

Decisions made this week:
- Use adaptive sampling algorithm A (configurable window=2min, min-rate=0.02) for the initial canary. Rationale: preserves tail traces while dropping noisy prefixes; benchmarked on replay.
- Dashboards will store a sample_rate label to enable correct normalization (Evelyn to own).
- Rollout schedule: 24h canaries per region, proceed if error rate delta < 0.1% and mean p95 latency change < 20ms.

Action items (owner / ETA / status):
- Lucas: land collector agg-fix patch and add heap-sample integration test. ETA: 2026-07-28. status: in_progress.
- Evelyn: update DS-24 and DS-09 to include sample_rate dimension; add guidance in dashboard doc. ETA: 2026-07-26. status: in_progress.
- Omar: add model_variant enrichment to cost-ingest lambda and open infra request for RBAC fix. ETA: 2026-07-25. status: blocked (RBAC).
- Asha: write short postmortem template for any canary regression and coordinate SRE on-call for 07/29 handoff. ETA: 2026-07-27. status: todo.

Open questions / risks:
- Do we have adequate budget alerts tied to token-cost changes when a model fallback occurs? Current alerts are token-volume only; need a per-route cost delta alert. (Action: Omar to propose alert rule by 07/26)
- How will tracing retention interact with the new sample labels (higher cardinality)? We risk higher index cost in Elasticsearch/ClickHouse; propose TTL tuning and a daily compaction job. (Lucas to prototype compaction job)
- Some Dedicated customers use a custom telemetry pipeline that strips sample_rate; need to reach out to Solutions Eng before global rollout. (Priya to email affected customers)

Experiment notes (trace-cost experiment):
- Hypothesis: adaptive sampling reduces trace ingestion cost by ~35% without materially impacting SLOs for tail-latency debugging.
- Test harness: replayed 72h request trace from prod into staging with adaptive sampler and baseline. Measured ingestion size, span counts, query performance on dashboards.
- Preliminary: ingestion decreased by 28% on replay, debug queries for top-100 endpoints had equivalent p95 trace capture in 91% of cases.
- Next: increase replay diversity (add long-run inference requests), then short canary on production.

Runbook snippets (short):
- Canary failure criteria: errors up > 0.5% absolute OR 5xx spike sustained for 5m OR dashboard query failures (timeout). If any: flip runtime.toggle.adaptive_sampling=false, notify #sre-observability and run postmortem template.
- Rollback steps: 1) flip toggle, 2) disable canary traffic routing, 3) escalate to on-call (pager duty), 4) capture heap/profile and timeline, 5) tag PRs and link to JIRA.

Notes to self / rough TODOs (very informal):
- Remember to add snippet for how to query sample_rate in Loki/trace-sql — put example query in dashboard docs.
- Add short blurb for support teammates: "If a customer reports missing traces for a route, check sample_rate label first before escalating."
- Slack thread to start: #obs-cost-alerts: propose per-route cost-delta alerting (Omar to start thread).

Outstanding links and references (copy/paste style):
- Collector PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/511
- Replay harness: gs://telemetry-replay/2026-07/prod-72h
- JIRA: OBS-342 (adaptive-sampling rollout), OBS-355 (dashboard sample-rate labels), OBS-361 (cost-ingest RBAC)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Trace+Sampling+Overview

Retro / pulses this week (quick takeaways):
- Good: replay harness proved useful for early signal. Team agile pairing helped find memory leak faster.
- Could be better: more coordination with Solutions Eng earlier, and clearer alerting for cost deltas.

If you're taking over the next shift (tag me in the doc):
- Check canary metrics dashboard (CANARY-ADAPTIVE-07-23), verify no error rate drift, ensure RBAC ticket (OBS-361) is being progressed.
- If you see query timeouts on the DS-* dashboards, run the quick compaction (script: infra/telemetry/scripts/compact_daily.sh) and alert infra.

End of notes. Keep this doc as ephemeral — will move key parts into the runbook once items resolve.

-- Asha
